- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥1.0) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly, especially after sharp spikes.
- When sentiment is negative (≤-1.0) or mixed, model often underestimates; adjust upward, particularly if recent price is trending down.
- Model frequently overreacts to short-term sentiment shifts — if sentiment flips from +1 to -1, reduce forecast by 2–5% immediately.
- Overshoots after price spikes (especially >75% above recent mean) are common; apply a “cool-down” correction: subtract 1–3% of forecast value if price > 75% above 14-day moving average.
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is >10% above recent 18-day average, reduce by 1–2% per day until convergence.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overestimate early in the forecast window (first 5–7 days); apply a 1–3% downward bias to first 5 days if sentiment is neutral or negative.
- If sentiment history shows repeated “+1, -1, +1” cycles, model tends to overcorrect — apply a 1–2% smoothing filter to avoid oscillation.
